I was looking for free syncing (or at minimum, a one-time upgrade fee, not a monthly or annual subscription), categorization, and flexibility to personalize it to my needs. I opted to try out Microsoft To Do to use as both a reminder and errands app. 

To Do allows me to add tasks under Lists (used by me like categories). You can have as many Lists as you like, and unlimited tasks within. Each task can have steps, which you can check off as you go. You can set up options to repeat recurring tasks, and add a notification at a time/date you choose. You can also add notes to the task. Your various lists/categories are down the left, along with My Day (all tasks due today) and Planned (all tasks that haven’t been closed).

What it’s missing: 
- My Day doesn’t show previous days’ tasks that are still outstanding. You can see that in Planned, as long as you select to view All tasks. 
-notification options. You get one notification, and then you can manually advance the notification to a different time/date if you choose. A reminder option would be handy. 
-Shake to undo. I can’t stress enough how handy this would be for iOS. The check boxes to close a task are biggish and easy to accidentally tap. Then the closed task moves into Completed at the bottom of the page, and if you didn’t happen to see what you tapped before it disappeared, you have to sort through the list (which can’t be sorted by Closed Date). This is a big frustration while I’m still getting used to the app. 
-moving a task to a different list. If you’re in the Bills list and hit Add a task, that task will be nested under Bills. If you meant for it to be under Kids instead, you either have to live with it, or delete it and re-enter where you want it to be. 
-Last date for recurring tasks. Being able to tell the app to repeat for X number of occurrences or until a certain date, seems like a no-brainer (especially since Outlook has had this option for years). 

The MS app forum does have a user suggestions area where you can add improvement suggestions or upvote others.

title: Mixed bag.
body:
Positives:

- Easy to visually separate tasks
- Incorporates subtasks for organizing more complex events.
- Cross platform
- Allows for some nice inbuilt functionality with Microsoft Planner and Outlook
- Allows you to invite users to shared lists

Negatives:

- Can’t embed a folder inside another folder (e.g., creating a “Daily Living” parent folder, with smaller folders inside such as “Health”, “Chores”, etc.).
- Shared lists don’t integrate with apple reminders. So there’s no way for your partner to say “Hey Siri, remind me to buy some broccoli”, and then have that populate on both your and their Microsoft To Do shared grocery lists.
- Siri integration and phrasing feels awkward (i.e., unnatural word choices).
- Can’t switch between a work and personal account without signing out and then re-signing in (huge deal breaker if I wanted to use this as my primary reminders/todo app).
- As with most Microsoft apps, it’s missing several features that are present on the windows desktop version.

title: It’s getting me to do things!
body:
I’ve tried reminders and such before, but they never seemed to work half as well as this one does.

I use a Windows 10 PC for both work and personal stuff. My problem was many checklist apps didn’t have good windows versions. I don’t look at my phone a ton, so any reminder that needed me to look at my phone went missing until it was too late in the day.

With the iOS app and the windows app combined, I’m able to add items from my phone, and complete things and see them updated on my desktop app. As well as vice versa.
The list is always displayed on one of the other monitors so it’s always there to remind me.

I know there are other apps that do that, but they were either too cumbersome or had a bad PC interface (if any at all) but this feels solid all around.

My only recommendations:
- the task complete sound hurts my ears it’s so bad. Please change it to something less painful.
-  (RESOLVED: thanks!) please allow us to add a widget to the iOS Home Screen so I don’t have to open the app to look at my lists

title: does the job, improvements possible
body:
I use both this and Wunderlist. I like how Wunderlist has the Today and This Week views, grouping items in their respective folders or categories. I would like to see that in To Do. I also find the date and time selectors cumbersome. Wunderlist is also cumbersome in its own way. 
   In To Do, I like the quick selectors of Today and Tomorrow; however Next Week should default to Monday and not Sunday, or provide option to choose what Next Week means. It would be good not to have to drill down to set a custom date, and then drill down to select a custom time. 
   One thing I appreciate is that sort setting is maintained. With this all said, To Do is simple yet valuable. I will still maintain Wunderlist because it is helpful as it keeps categories separated for the Today list, but the bulk of my tasks will be in this app.

body:
I am a huge Apple fan boy and so naturally I will usually be using the proprietary Reminders app that comes stock on IOS devices BUT! When I first tried this app on my PC (I don’t like macs) I fell in love with it and have it on every device now, and I’m glad to say I am very happy with it.

title: Stripped down wunderlist microsofted junk
body:
I'm a wunderlist user of 4+ years, thousands of tasks done, this new app is barebones and opposite of what an amazing wunderlist app is. 

Stupid generic "we can't think of anything original" checkmark app icon is bothering me. 

No weekly view. I live here, don't take away my home. Instead in this app you get "My Day" with today's date. Today's date? You are not a calendar app. What's next added? Weather, fb, twitter, calculator, DO TO DO LISTS only please!

Useless background to list title, why is this taking up HALF of my screen? I know what the title is, and nobody needs a generic pointless picture behind it, I NEED TO GET STUFF DONE FOR PETES SAKE NOT LOOK AT BACKGROUND CLIPART!!

New "to do" item is added to bottom of list, this small function is a deal breaker for me. I need new items to appear up top. It may seem small or insignificant, but to me it makes a huge difference. This is probably the main reason, for me at least, for using Wunderlist and not Apple Reminders. 

No red star ribbon to push items up top. 

No folders. I NEED dis. 

No task sharing. 

If this app is what we're getting as a replacement, I will buy a separate iPhone to use for everything else and use only this one for my Wunderlist! Forever not closing the app or turning it off or updating or signing out!!
